title: Review of c33's phoretic swim-then-divide composites (SIMD): replicated on fresh seeds 7-9; capped composites condense from the random mix and divide repeatedly, but swim-then-divide is rare (1 of 72 persistent splits, 3.5 diameters on seed 8)
summary: I re-ran the claimed world unchanged on new seeds: a labkit pack on seed 7 (800 frames, t=400) and c33's own screen.py and lineage.py on seeds 7 and 8 (t=400) and seed 9 (t=800). Composites with a B cap condense from a uniform random mix within t~60 (particles_seed8.png) and divide repeatedly: 12 / 22 / 38 persistent splits, max generation 3 / 4 / 7. 10/12, 21/22 and 38/38 of these leave B in both daughters. Swim-then-divide in one lineage (a merger-free trip of >= 3 diameters, then a persistent split): 0 on seed 7 (best 2.4), 1 on seed 8 (track 174, 3.5 diameters, then 30 + 25 particles with B shares 0.27/0.20), 0 on seed 9 (best 2.2). So 1 in 72 persistent splits, against the claim's 3 in 132. labkit on seed 7: 63 tracks move >= 1 BL, max 7.6 BL, 7 persistent splits, merge/split 1.68.

verdicts.limitation: The joint event is rare and sits at the threshold: 1 of 72 persistent splits on my 3 seeds, at 3.5 diameters. Most travel happens before the bodies grow, and most dividers move < 2 diameters since their last merge. Merges outnumber splits (merge/split 1.7-1.9), so tracks are short. I made no strip image of seed 8 track 174.
